title: Input, Output & Console Formatting
description: I/O handles reading user input and formatting stream outputs to stdout, stderr, and files.

codeExamples.python:
name = input('Enter name: ') if False else 'Alice'
age = 25
print(f'User {name} is {age} years old.')
print('Raw bytes:', 'Hello'.encode('utf-8'))

quiz.question: What data type does Python's built-in `input()` function ALWAYS return?
options: String (`str`). Even if the user types a number like 42, `input()` returns `'42'`. Cast using `int()` or `float()`.
quiz.explanation: Python `input()` reads input line-by-line from sys.stdin as a string object. Type casting is required for numeric computations.

interviewQuestions.q: 01. What is the difference between `sys.stdout.write()` and `print()` in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: `print()` automatically adds a trailing newline (`\n`) and handles argument string conversion. `sys.stdout.write()` writes raw strings directly to stdout stream without newline additions.

interviewQuestions.q: 02. What is Stream Buffer Flushing and what does `flush=True` do?
interviewQuestions.a: I/O streams buffer data in RAM before writing to disk or terminal. `flush=True` forces the OS to immediately flush the buffer out to hardware without waiting for newline or buffer overflow.

interviewQuestions.q: 03. What is the difference between `stdout` vs `stderr`?
interviewQuestions.a: `stdout` (Standard Output) streams normal program data (file descriptor 1). `stderr` (Standard Error) streams error logs and warnings (file descriptor 2), preventing error messages from corrupting piped output.

interviewQuestions.q: 04. Why is fast I/O (`sys.stdin.read().split()`) required in competitive programming?
interviewQuestions.a: Built-in `input()` has high per-line overhead. `sys.stdin.read()` buffers all input into a single RAM string, running up to 10-20x faster.

interviewQuestions.q: 05. How does `f-string` formatting (`f"{val:.2f}"`) handle floating-point precision?
interviewQuestions.a: Format specifier `.2f` rounds and formats floats to 2 decimal places (e.g. `f"{3.14159:.2f}"` -> `'3.14'`).

interviewQuestions.q: 06. What is EOF (End of File) and how do you handle EOF exceptions in Python?
interviewQuestions.a: EOF signifies no more data remains in an input stream. Catch `EOFError` in a `try...except` block or check `while line := sys.stdin.readline():`.

interviewQuestions.q: 07. What is Command Line I/O Piping (`|`) and Redirection (`>` / `<`)?
interviewQuestions.a: `>` redirects stdout to a file (`python script.py > output.txt`). `<` feeds a file to stdin (`python script.py < input.txt`). `|` pipes stdout of process A to stdin of process B.

interviewQuestions.q: 08. How does `print()` handle `sep` and `end` parameters?
interviewQuestions.a: `sep` specifies delimiter string between multiple arguments (default space `' '`). `end` specifies string printed at the end (default newline `'\n'`).

interviewQuestions.q: 09. What is String Interpolation vs Concatenation for output formatting?
interviewQuestions.a: String interpolation (`f"{a} {b}"`) compiles to optimized string formatting bytecode, avoiding multi-object creation caused by string concatenation (`a + ' ' + b`).

interviewQuestions.q: 10. What is `Scanner` vs `BufferedReader` in Java I/O performance?
interviewQuestions.a: `BufferedReader` reads large 8KB byte chunks from stream into memory, outperforming `Scanner` which parses tokens with heavy regex overhead.

interviewQuestions.q: 11. How does `std::cin` and `std::cout` synchronization work in C++?
interviewQuestions.a: By default `std::cin` flushes `std::cout`. Disabling synchronization using `std::ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false); std::cin.tie(NULL);` drastically accelerates C++ I/O.

interviewQuestions.q: 12. What is Non-Blocking I/O vs Blocking I/O?
interviewQuestions.a: Blocking I/O halts thread execution until input data arrives. Non-Blocking I/O returns immediately if no data is ready, used in asynchronous event loops (Node.js, asyncio).

interviewQuestions.q: 13. What is File I/O buffering modes (Unbuffered, Line-Buffered, Block-Buffered)?
interviewQuestions.a: Unbuffered writes immediately. Line-buffered flushes on `\n` (terminals). Block-buffered flushes when 4KB/8KB RAM buffer fills up (disk files).

interviewQuestions.q: 14. How do you print ANSI Escape Codes for colored terminal output?
interviewQuestions.a: ANSI codes like `\033[31mRed Text\033[0m` instruct terminal emulators to change text color, background, or cursor position.

interviewQuestions.q: 15. What is `repr()` vs `str()` when printing objects?
interviewQuestions.a: `str()` returns a user-friendly string representation. `repr()` returns an unambiguous developer representation showing object type and exact state.

interviewQuestions.q: 16. How does `sys.argv` parse command-line input arguments?
interviewQuestions.a: `sys.argv` is a list where `sys.argv[0]` is script name and `sys.argv[1:]` contains passed positional argument strings.

interviewQuestions.q: 17. What is `getpass` module used for in Python CLI apps?
interviewQuestions.a: `getpass.getpass()` prompts for user passwords without echoing characters to terminal screen.

interviewQuestions.q: 18. What is `struct` module in Python binary I/O?
interviewQuestions.a: `struct.pack()` and `struct.unpack()` convert Python values to/from C binary struct bytes for raw network stream I/O.

interviewQuestions.q: 19. How does `printf` specifier `%d`, `%s`, `%f`, `%x` work in C/C++/Java?
interviewQuestions.a: %d = decimal integer, %s = string, %f = float, %x = hexadecimal integer.

interviewQuestions.q: 20. What are production best practices for Console and Logging I/O?
interviewQuestions.a: Use structured logging framework (`logging` module, JSON logs) instead of plain `print()`, write errors to `stderr`, and explicitly flush streams when logging critical crashes.
